relations.subject: backup:full-backup
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (tradesOffAgainst) - same comparative-strategy shape as the vector-index tradeoffs this predicate was first minted for: opposite strengths (restore performance vs. time/storage cost)
relations.evidence: Full bucket backups provide the best restore performance but take the most time to complete, require the most storage, and can be demanding on cluster resources... Incremental backups include the data that has changed since the last Scheduled backup. They take less time and storage space to create than a Full backup.

relations.subject: backup:incremental-backup
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresPriorExecutionOf) - a hard restore-ordering dependency, not just a recommendation
relations.evidence: Incremental bucket backups depend on Full bucket backups to be restored. The Full backup is always restored first, followed by the incremental backups.

relations.subject: backup:bucket-backup
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (gatedByBillingPlan) - object generalized here to a policy choice rather than a plan:* concept, since the tradeoff is user-selected and explicitly framed in cost terms (TCO vs RPO), not a fixed plan-tier limit
relations.evidence: You can select a cost-optimized retention policy to manage bucket backups, and provide a trade-off between total cost of ownership (TCO) and the recovery point objective (RPO).

notable_absence.finding: This concept/reference page never states a capella-role:* or support-plan gate itself - all access-control statements for bucket backups (Project Owner / Organization Owner) live on the companion procedural pages (manage-backup.md, manage-restore.md), not here. This page is purely descriptive of mechanics, retention, and cost, consistent with its reference-page framing.

cross_component_finding: Directly relevant to this batch's hypothesis: bucket-backup access control is completely absent from this page and, per manage-backup.json/manage-restore.json, is gated purely by capella-role:* (Project Owner, with Organization Owner implying it) - no support-plan or billing-plan gate appears anywhere on the bucket-backup surface for WHO can back up or restore. The only plan/billing-shaped gate found on the bucket-backup surface is a feature-availability one, not a role one (see manage-backup.json's free-tier finding).
cross_product_finding: As part of your Capella bucket backup storage costs, you are charged for the storage that a downloadable backup file uses... Using the download URL incurs data transfer charges. Confirms backup storage and egress genuinely carry direct billing consequences (this round's hypothesis framing), but the gating mechanism observed is cost/usage-based billing, not a distinct support-plan or billing-plan access gate - anyone with the requisite capella-role:* can incur these costs; there is no plan tier that blocks or unlocks bucket-backup download.
